questions.source: Safran. (2021). 4 reasons why risk models are crucial for successful project management. Retrieved August 18, 2021, from https://www.safran.com/blog/4-reasons-why-risk-models-are-crucial-for-successful-project-management

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in risk management

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about risk retention groups:

options.A: They are limited to the medical industry.
options.B: They can be located anywhere in the world.
options.C: They are limited to writing liability coverage.
options.D: They can write any insurance coverage.

questions.explanation: They are limited to writing liability coverage. Risk retention groups are a type of captive insurance company. They are limited to providing only liability coverage to members of the group. Captive insurance companies can write any type of coverage and can be located anywhere in the world, while risk retention groups are limited to the United States. Neither risk retention groups nor captive insurance companies are limited to the medical industry, although they both do provide coverage for these groups.
questions.source: Lipscomb & Pitts Insurance. (2017, August 24). Risk retention group or a captive: What's the difference? Retrieved August 17, 2021, from https://lpinsurance.com/blog/risk-retention-or-captive/

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss legal considerations affecting risk management

questions.question: While a U.S. company conducts business in Chile, the value of the Chilean peso fluctuates and depreciates against the U.S. dollar. This is an example of which of the following types of risk:
questions.explanation: Foreign exchange. Foreign exchange risk occurs when an investment's value changes due to fluctuations in the currency exchange rate. Geopolitical risk occurs when a government suddenly changes its trade policies. Security and fraud risk involves issues like data breaches and identity theft. Competition risk refers to a business's competitors, which are not mentioned in this scenario.
questions.source: Beers, B. (2020, May 4). Top risks for international businesses. Retrieved August 20, 2021, from https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/06/internationalfinancerisks.asp

performanceIndicator.text: Describe international considerations affecting risk management

questions.question: After a power outage, the point-of-sale software at Leif's Fine Treats malfunctions, meaning the store is unable to complete any customer purchases. What type of planning would be most effective in this situation?
questions.explanation: Contingency. Contingency planning includes backup plans and crisis responses for a variety of scenarios. A contingency plan would help Leif's Fine Treats determine the best way to proceed. Tactical planning involves specific, measurable, short-term goals. A strategic plan looks at the big picture and defines a company's overall goals. Operational plans are used to document processes on a day-to-day basis.
questions.source: Pingboard. (2020, April 27). Organizational planning guide: Types of plans, steps, and examples. Retrieved August 13, 2021, from https://pingboard.com/blog/organizational-planning-guide-types-of-plans-steps-and-examples/

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of managerial planning

questions.question: Which of the following is a barrier to effective planning:
questions.explanation: Focusing on controllable variables. It's important for managers to consider both variables they can control, such as product development, as well as variables they cannot control, including external factors like the economy. Focusing purely on controllable variables is a barrier to successful planning. Linking planning goals to long-term objectives, relying on quality information, and committing to the process are all characteristics of effective planning.
questions.source: CliffsNotes. (2020). Identifying barriers to planning. Retrieved August 17, 2021, from https://www.cliffsnotes.com/study-guides/principles-of-management/organizational-planning/identifying-barriers-to-planning

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of managerial planning

questions.question: Which of the following management functions must occur before organizing:
questions.explanation: Planning. Organizing is the management function that includes setting up the way a business's work will be done. It follows the planning function. After a manager has created a plan, they need to arrange the business's employees, resources, policies, and procedures to put the plan into action. Staffing, controlling, and directing do not have to occur before organizing.
questions.source: LAP-SM-064—Put it All Together (Managerial Considerations in Organizing)

performanceIndicator.text: Explain managerial considerations in organizing

questions.question: Screening potential new employees includes which of the following responsibilities:

options.A: Weeding out applicants who do not meet minimum job requirements
options.B: Partnering with outside employment agencies and participating in job fairs
options.C: Extending the job offer with specific terms and conditions
options.D: Providing information about company policies and procedures

questions.explanation: Weeding out applicants who do not meet minimum job requirements. When a pool of potential candidates has been identified, managers begin the process of screening the applicants and selecting which ones to interview. They begin by "weeding out" (usually with the help of applicant tracking software) those applicants who do not meet the minimum job requirements or have not satisfactorily completed the application process. Recruiting involves partnering with outside employment agencies and participating in job fairs. Extending the job offer with specific terms and conditions is part of selecting. Onboarding involves providing information about company policies and procedures.
questions.source: LAP-SM-065—Dream Team Maker (Staffing)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: To develop their human resources management strategy, successful managers consider the organizational dimensions that will affect their plan, including factors such as organizational culture. Which of the following questions would be most useful when gathering information about organizational culture:

options.A: How do employees interact with each other?
options.B: How does the company move forward?
options.C: How are jobs grouped and arranged?
options.D: How should current policies be modified?

questions.explanation: How do employees interact with each other? Organizational culture is the "personality" of the organization. Answers to questions like "How do employees interact with each other?" tell managers about the culture of their organization and give them clues about which types of HR management strategies will work best. "How does the company move forward?" addresses the company's mission and vision, both of which can influence mangers' choice of human resources management strategy. "How are jobs grouped and arranged?" provides information about the organizational structure. "How should current policies be modified?" provides insight about existing human resources policies and practices. Managers can gain a lot of insight into developing HR management strategies by carefully observing the benefits and disadvantages of current practices.
questions.source: LAP-SM-065—Dream Team Maker (Staffing)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: Kelli asks Ricardo to put together a report for her upcoming meeting. Kelli is
questions.explanation: Directing. Directing is the management function of providing guidance to workers to achieve goals. When instructing Ricardo to put together a report, Kelli is engaged in directing. In this example, Kelli is not staffing, organizing, or planning.
questions.source: LAP-SM-066—Take Action (Managerial Considerations in Directing)

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss managerial considerations in directing

questions.question: Kevon works in quality assurance, which means he is responsible for inspecting the production line while it is in operation. What type of managerial control is Kevon exercising?
questions.explanation: Concurrent. Concurrent controls are those that monitor and control performance while it is occurring. A quality assurance manager inspecting a production line while it is in operation is an example of concurrent control. Feedforward controls are those that attempt to monitor and control performance before it occurs. Feedback controls are those that monitor and control performance after it has already occurred. Performance control is not a recognized type of managerial control.
questions.source: LAP-SM-400—Measure Up! (Managerial Control)

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of managerial control (control process, types of control, what is controlled)

questions.question: Which of the following demonstrates business innovation:

options.A: Xavi listens to a startup business podcast.
options.D: Myesha attends a creative design conference.

questions.explanation: Tessa introduces more sustainable packaging. Businesses must innovate to stay competitive, which includes creating new products or services, improving existing processes, and implementing other methods to increase efficiency and improve the company's bottom line. Tessa is contributing to business innovation by introducing more sustainable packaging. While listening to a podcast, reviewing campaign results, and attending a conference may spark new ideas, they are not direct examples of innovation.
questions.source: Green, N. (2019, October 11). What is business innovation and why is it important? Retrieved August 19, 2021, from https://www.wework.com/ideas/professional-development/creativity-culture/what-is-business-innovation

performanceIndicator.text: Describe relationship among innovation, learning, and change

questions.question: Polar Pops introduced a new sales strategy for its nationwide franchises. Sales manager Luna sets reasonable goals for her team, schedules hands-on training, and provides constructive feedback. In the ADKAR change management model, which stage is Luna practicing?
questions.explanation: Ability. The ADKAR model of change is a tool for understanding, creating, and adapting to change. The acronym stands for Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, and Reinforcement. In the model, Ability means ensuring employees have confidence in their capability to change. To build this confidence, management can use hands-on training and practice runs, set reasonable goals, and provide detailed, constructive feedback. The Reinforcement stage emphasizes performance measures, recognition, and rewards. Awareness refers to informing employees about the change. Desire emphasizes building support for the change.
questions.source: Malhotra, G. (2019, November 21). ADKAR model: What is it and how to use it? Retrieved August 13, 2021, from https://whatfix.com/blog/adkar-model-what-is-it-and-how-to-use-it/

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of change management

questions.question: Which phase in the change management life cycle encourages top-down and bottom-up communication about the need for change to encourage adoption of the change and align the organization's overall response?
questions.explanation: Engage. Phase two in the change management life cycle encourages top-down and bottom-up communication about the need for change to encourage adoption of the change and align the organization's overall response. This phase is centered on engaging people. The Identify phase involves communicating the need for change in a clear, organized way. This phase compares the current state to the desired future state of the organization. The Implement phase changes the strategies identified in the Identify and Engage phases into tactics for progressing to the future state of the organization. While reviewing changes is a helpful strategy, it is not a recognized phase of the change management life cycle.
questions.source: TwentyEighty Strategy Execution. (2015). The change management life cycle: How to involve your people to ensure success at every state. Retrieved January 24, 2022, from https://paperzz.com/doc/6755421/the-change-management-life-cycle

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the change-management lifecycle

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between people and change management:

options.A: Change happens one person at a time.
options.B: Good employees do as they are told.

questions.explanation: Change happens one person at a time. Change management is necessary because organizational change occurs on a person-by-person basis. The people at the organization make changes, not the organization itself. Successful organizational change is the cumulative result of individual actions. Employees may be instructed to do something illegal or unethical, in which case they would not follow those directions. Rapid changes would lower employee morale. People do not embrace change automatically—in fact, they often resist change at first.
questions.source: Prosci. (n.d.). What is change management and how does it work? Retrieved August 20, 2021, from https://www.prosci.com/resources/articles/what-is-change-management-and-how-does-it-work

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the change-management lifecycle
